title: Check yourself: Fast mode, thinking with tools, and thinking's effect on caching

questions.stem: A chat feature on Opus 5.5 streams long answers to people watching the text appear, and the team wants it to arrive sooner without a change of tier or effort. Which option does the page support?

options.text: Fast mode, at the standard price and on every cloud platform
options.says: Ruled out because "it is not available on Claude Platform on AWS or partner-operated cloud platforms".

options.text: Fast mode, at twice the standard price, on the first-party API
options.says: The page says fast mode "is available on the Claude API (first-party) only" and prices it at twice the standard rate.

options.text: A lower effort level, with a reduced price and shorter replies
options.says: Ruled out because the table gives "fast mode (Opus only)" to streaming, and gives lowering the effort to "Too slow to finish".

options.text: A batch, at half the price and with the replies delivered sooner
options.says: Ruled out because "Fast mode is not available with the Batch API."

origin.section: Fast mode: faster output, higher price

questions.stem: A tool loop runs four calls for one user question. The team sets reasoning on for the first call and off for the last three to save tokens. What happens?

options.text: The API treats each call as its own turn and accepts the new setting
options.says: Ruled out because "A tool-use loop is one assistant turn."

options.text: The API returns a 400 for the first changed request and stops the loop
options.says: Ruled out by that same sentence, since the stated behaviour is "silently disables thinking for that request" and not a 400.

options.text: The API keeps the first setting for the whole turn and ignores the rest
options.says: Ruled out because the changed request is the one that loses thinking: "silently disables thinking for that request".

options.text: The API silently disables thinking on the altered steps, without error
options.says: The page says the API does not error: it "silently disables thinking for that request".

questions.stem: A team lowers the effort for later turns of a long conversation that relies on a cached document. What follows?

options.text: The stored tools and system are invalidated, but the messages stay valid
options.says: Ruled out because the messages are the part that "always discards the cached messages" names, while tools and system are model-specific.

options.text: The stored messages are invalidated, so the text is written again
options.says: The page says changing the thinking mode or the effort "always discards the cached messages".

options.text: The cache stays valid, because effort is applied after the prefix
options.says: Ruled out because the resolved configuration "is rendered into the prompt", so it is not applied after the prefix.

options.text: The cache is invalidated only when the effort is raised above the default
options.says: Ruled out because the messages are discarded on any change: "always discards the cached messages".
